objective:
Round 2 of #18 on your own branch (head 5904e94). The reviewer found one major and three minors you own. Fix all four:
1. MAJOR src/server.ts: AbortSignal.timeout(15_000) also aborts the body stream, so a client slower than ~50 KB/s has the full-file response cut off at 15 s. Make the 15 s limit cover only the time until the upstream response headers arrive: an AbortController plus a setTimeout that is cleared as soon as fetch() resolves (and on throw). After that the body streams with no overall limit; if the client disconnects, the upstream body must still be cancelled (it is today; keep it).
2. src/server.ts isGithubHttps: also require the pathname to match /^\/[^/]+\/[^/]+\/releases\/download\/[^/]+\/[^/]+\.mp4$/ (a release asset only, no other github.com page).
3. One rule for "this snapshot has a playable video", used by both page and server: export a single predicate (e.g. demoVideoSource(url): boolean) from src/page.ts with the rule from item 2 plus https/github.com/no port/no userinfo, and have server.ts import it instead of its own isGithubHttps. The page draws the <video> only when it returns true; otherwise the card shows its text with no player (the text is unchanged).
4. Tests: an upstream body that errors mid-stream (server stays up, /healthz still 200); a client disconnect mid-stream cancels the upstream body; a body that takes longer than the header timeout to finish still completes (use fake timers or an injectable timeout ms via AppOptions, e.g. demoHeaderTimeoutMs, default 15000); the log never contains the upstream URL, a release-assets host, or the Authorization header (capture logs with a stream on Fastify logger option or app.log spy); a non-release github.com path is 404 and draws no <video>.
